h1: Adelphi Forty-Nine — Spacious Suites, Full Kitchen · The Go-To Stay Near Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital
intro: If you need to be close to Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital — whether you're a patient or a family member keeping watch — Adelphi Forty-Nine is the most practical choice on this soi. The hospital sits roughly 450 metres away; an unhurried walk of under 6 minutes. Better still, the hotel runs a free shuttle directly to the hospital every day, so you don't need to think twice. Every one of its 86 rooms is a suite of 50–58 sqm with a full kitchen, a washing machine and a private balcony — the kind of space that makes a two-week medical stay genuinely liveable. Opened in 2015 on the quiet stretch of Soi 49. From approx. THB 2,600/night. Scored 9.1 from 380 Booking.com reviews.

body.html: Adelphi Forty-Nine was built around a single idea: a proper home away from home. Every room is a suite — not a standard hotel room with a kettle and a mini-bar, but a fully equipped 50- or 58-sqm apartment with an induction cooker, refrigerator, microwave, a complete set of cookware and a washing machine. For anyone facing a multi-week hospital stay, those details matter enormously. You can cook the food the doctor recommends, wash clothes without hunting for a laundromat, and recover without the background noise of a lobby buzzing with weekend check-ins.

The hotel's strongest selling point is its relationship with Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital. The hospital entrance on Soi 49 is about 450 metres from the front desk — a flat, straightforward walk of under 6 minutes. On days when walking isn't practical, the hotel's complimentary shuttle runs to the hospital daily, as well as to BTS Thong Lo. Guests who came specifically for treatment at Samitivej mention the shuttle repeatedly in reviews, often describing it as one of the reasons they'd return or recommend the property to others in the same situation.

"We stayed two weeks while my mother had treatment at Samitivej. The staff were extraordinary — the shuttle to the hospital made everything so much easier, the room was spotless, and we could cook proper meals. We didn't feel like hotel guests; we felt looked after."

The four room categories are straightforward: One Bedroom Suite (50 sqm) and the wider One Bedroom Premier Suite (58 sqm), each available in a standard or Executive tier. Both have a separated living area, floor-to-ceiling windows, a Japanese-style electronic toilet, a deep soaking bathtub and a rainfall shower. The Executive tier adds in-room check-in, a 4 pm late check-out and laundry discounts — worth considering if you're staying several weeks. Cleanliness scores 9.6/10 on Booking.com, the highest of any category, and most guests describe the rooms as feeling genuinely cared for.

The staff are the other pillar of the property's reputation. Booking.com guests score them 9.4/10, and TripAdvisor reviewers frequently name individual team members by name — the kind of recognition you only earn when the service feels personal rather than scripted. The hotel also offers a small perk: decline housekeeping for the day and receive a complimentary drink instead. The seventh-floor pool opens at 6 am — a decent option for light exercise during a recovery stay — and the TechnoGym fitness centre shares the same floor, running until 10 pm.

What you should know before booking: Soi 49 runs deep into the neighbourhood, and the walk to BTS stations is real — roughly 10–12 minutes to Thong Lo, slightly more to Phrom Phong. The free shuttle covers this for most guests, and the hotel offers free car parking if you're driving. Some reviews note traffic noise and air-conditioning sound in rooms facing the soi, particularly at night. The breakfast buffet is functional rather than lavish — a point a few reviewers flag — and the WiFi, while fast in public areas, can be inconsistent in certain rooms on upper floors.

The bottom line is uncomplicated: Adelphi Forty-Nine is the most purpose-built option for a Samitivej Sukhumvit visit in this price range. The combination of proximity, a free hospital shuttle, spacious apartment-style rooms and genuinely attentive staff adds up to something that's hard to replicate in a conventional hotel. Rates start around THB 2,600/night for a 50 sqm suite — reasonable for a 4-star property on Sukhumvit, and very good value if you're staying a fortnight or more.

honestSummary: Adelphi Forty-Nine is the most practical base for a Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital visit in its price range. The free hospital shuttle, full-kitchen suites and genuinely caring staff are a strong package for patients and caregivers alike. The caveats are real but minor: the soi walk to BTS is longer than some guests expect, and a handful of rooms pick up street noise at night.
honestChecks: If you plan to use the BTS every day without a car — the walk to Thong Lo or Phrom Phong is 10–12 minutes, not 5. Use the free shuttle for morning trips; budget THB 50–80 for a Grab at other times, or ask about the shuttle schedule at check-in.
If you're a light sleeper — rooms facing Soi 49 can catch traffic and air-conditioning noise. Request a high-floor, inward-facing room when booking; the difference is significant.

If you want a full hotel-restaurant experience — the breakfast here is simple and the on-site dining options are limited. The strength of this property is the apartment kitchen; Soi 49 also has good local restaurants within a short walk.

tips.title: Register for the hospital shuttle at check-in
tips.body: Let the front desk know your appointment schedule at Samitivej when you arrive. They'll confirm the shuttle timing and pick-up point — particularly useful for early-morning appointments or post-procedure days when you don't want to manage a Grab.

tips.title: Use the BTS shuttle — it saves more than you think
tips.body: The free shuttle to BTS Thong Lo runs in the mornings. From Thong Lo you can reach Siam, Asok or EmQuartier in minutes. Factor this into your schedule and you'll rarely need to pay for a taxi.

tips.title: Stock the kitchen on arrival
tips.body: There's a supermarket and a local market within easy walking distance on Soi 49. Stocking up on day one means you have full control over your meals — important if you're on a post-procedure diet or simply want to manage costs during a long stay.

tips.title: The pool at 6 am is yours alone
tips.body: The 7th-floor pool opens at 6 am and is almost always empty before 8 am. The Bangkok skyline at that hour is worth setting an alarm for — and light swimming is one of the better recovery exercises a doctor is likely to approve.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Adelphi Forty-Nine Bangkok

faq.q: How far is Adelphi Forty-Nine from Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital? Is there a shuttle?
faq.a: The hotel is approximately 450 metres from Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital — a flat, straightforward walk of under 6 minutes along Soi 49. The hotel also operates a complimentary shuttle to the hospital every day, so on days when walking isn't convenient (after a procedure, with luggage, in heavy rain) you're covered without paying for a taxi.

faq.q: Where exactly is Adelphi Forty-Nine and how do I reach BTS?
faq.a: The hotel is at 16 Soi Sukhumvit 49, Khlong Tan Nuea, Watthana, Bangkok 10110. BTS Thong Lo (Sukhumvit line) is about 630 m away — a 10-minute walk, or use the hotel's free shuttle that runs to the station. BTS Phrom Phong is roughly 900 m in the other direction. Free car parking is available for guests who drive.

faq.q: What room types does Adelphi Forty-Nine offer, and what are the prices?
faq.a: All 86 rooms are suites. The One Bedroom Suite (50 sqm) starts from around THB 2,600/night with a full kitchen, washing machine and balcony. The One Bedroom Premier Suite (58 sqm) adds floor-to-ceiling city views and more living space, from roughly THB 3,200. Executive versions of both tiers include in-room check-in and a 4 pm late check-out. Prices vary by season — December rates are typically the highest.

faq.q: Is Adelphi Forty-Nine suitable for a long medical stay or caregiving visit?
faq.a: It's purpose-built for exactly this. Every room has a complete kitchen (induction cooker, refrigerator, microwave, full cookware), a washing machine, daily housekeeping and a free hospital shuttle. The Executive tier adds late check-out and laundry discounts for guests staying several weeks. The staff are accustomed to guests with medical needs and are noted for being particularly attentive and patient.

faq.q: Does Adelphi Forty-Nine have a swimming pool?
faq.a: Yes — an outdoor rooftop pool on the 7th floor, open 6:00 AM to 10:00 PM, with views over the Bangkok skyline. The TechnoGym fitness centre is on the same floor. The pool is not competition-sized but is a very good amenity for light exercise during a recovery stay.

faq.q: Who is Adelphi Forty-Nine best suited for?
faq.a: The property is best for patients and caregivers at Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital, long-stay business travellers who want apartment-style living, and families needing space and a kitchen. It's less ideal for guests who want to walk to BTS multiple times a day without a car, or who are looking for a full-service hotel restaurant experience.
